plain_explanation:
Liam Lawson's car 30 for Visa Cash App Racing Bulls has been disqualified from the results of Q2 qualifying at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

The car failed to comply with Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the F1 Regulations. After crossing the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, Lawson did not lift off the power immediately. This meant the car could not achieve the regulated "step down" — the required rate of reduction in MGUK deployment (the staged reduction in power from the electrical motor).

The team argued that this breach gave no performance advantage. The Stewards rejected this argument. They said that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused if no performance advantage is gained. They also noted that the regulations require a car to comply with them at all times during an event.

Although the team self-disclosed the breach, the Stewards said there are many precedents that require disqualification when a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations, regardless of other circumstances.
